Cyber Security News
2026-06-02 2 use cases 1 technique 2 kill-chain phases detected

A newly analyzed remote access trojan called PHANTOMPULSE has drawn serious attention for its advanced approach to compromising Windows systems. The malware is the final-stage payload in a broader attack chain known as REF6598, a threat cluster actively targeting the cryptocurrency sector. Actions on Objectives
Likely
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code.
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("70bbb38b70fd836d66e8166ec27be9aa8535b3876596fc80c45e3de4ce327980", "33dacf9f854f636216e5062ca252df8e5bed652efd78b86512f5b868b11ee70f") or SHA1 in~ ("70bbb38b70fd836d66e8166ec27be9aa8535b3876596fc80c45e3de4ce327980", "33dacf9f854f636216e5062ca252df8e5bed652efd78b86512f5b868b11ee70f") or MD5 in~ ("70bbb38b70fd836d66e8166ec27be9aa8535b3876596fc80c45e3de4ce327980", "33dacf9f854f636216e5062ca252df8e5bed652efd78b86512f5b868b11ee70f")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("70bbb38b70fd836d66e8166ec27be9aa8535b3876596fc80c45e3de4ce327980", "33dacf9f854f636216e5062ca252df8e5bed652efd78b86512f5b868b11ee70f") or SHA1 in~ ("70bbb38b70fd836d66e8166ec27be9aa8535b3876596fc80c45e3de4ce327980", "33dacf9f854f636216e5062ca252df8e5bed652efd78b86512f5b868b11ee70f") or MD5 in~ ("70bbb38b70fd836d66e8166ec27be9aa8535b3876596fc80c45e3de4ce327980", "33dacf9f854f636216e5062ca252df8e5bed652efd78b86512f5b868b11ee70f")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["70bbb38b70fd836d66e8166ec27be9aa8535b3876596fc80c45e3de4ce327980", "33dacf9f854f636216e5062ca252df8e5bed652efd78b86512f5b868b11ee70f"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0b

    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.file_name, Filesystem.file_hash

Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2025-48595")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2025-48595")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2025-48595")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve

Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2025-8088", "CVE-2018-20250")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2025-8088", "CVE-2018-20250")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("1794369214b7f62e70a0485e61335c61", "8e1624d110c090ff57d4b493a9107c66") or SHA1 in~ ("1794369214b7f62e70a0485e61335c61", "8e1624d110c090ff57d4b493a9107c66") or MD5 in~ ("1794369214b7f62e70a0485e61335c61", "8e1624d110c090ff57d4b493a9107c66")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("1794369214b7f62e70a0485e61335c61", "8e1624d110c090ff57d4b493a9107c66") or SHA1 in~ ("1794369214b7f62e70a0485e61335c61", "8e1624d110c090ff57d4b493a9107c66") or MD5 in~ ("1794369214b7f62e70a0485e61335c61", "8e1624d110c090ff57d4b493a9107c66")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["1794369214b7f62e70a0485e61335c61", "8e1624d110c090ff57d4b493a9107c66"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`

    [| tstats summariesonly=false count

         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"

     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",

                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")

| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user

[LLM] DriveSurge zTDS loader script injection (t.js?site=<id>) outbound Delivery High
Hunts for browsers fetching the DriveSurge JavaScript loader served from compromised sites via the 't.js?site=<id>' URI pattern, or contacting the campaign's injection/TDS domains. This is the earliest visible step of the kill chain before any payload is served. Rationale: Anchored on the campaign-unique 't.js?site=<id>' loader URI pattern plus the 8 injection/TDS hostnames and 4 IPs explicitly listed in the article and SilentPush IOC drop. Restricting to browser-initiated traffic strips out scanner/researcher noise. Cross-checked against: • https://www.silentpush.com/blog/drivesurge/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1189/
ATT&CKT1189 T1583.008

[LLM] FakeUpdates 'Browser Update.exe' drop from ZIP in user-writable path Installation High
Detects execution of the campaign's fake Firefox/Chrome/etc. installer binary 'Browser Update.exe' or its sibling DLLs from Downloads/%TEMP%, especially when the parent is a browser or archive utility. Targets the FakeUpdates payload stage described in the Silent Push report. Rationale: Article explicitly names 'Browser Update.exe' as the fake-Firefox payload bundled in a ZIP with DLLs, and provides four SHA256s for the campaign's stagers. Filename + hash + user-writable-path are all article-grounded high-fidelity anchors. Cross-checked against: • https://www.silentpush.com/blog/drivesurge/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1036/005/
ATT&CKT1204.002 T1036.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
let CampaignHashes = dynamic(["90aecb370dfb1a99a1f7de0a9c6842ab1b664521fddea16b0ec9a91f322646fc","7aa15de93cf85729ddf970e8d7897f69ece3ca29608f73e784a9ba40c9cea18d","8ecc7108cd679316bf5900e84f19b256dc399902cdede646493f502ac872cc1a","e1ce4e6222396a58d13dddfe64c1dd21f1632bcbe11d1867d44bab4fc646883a"]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where FileName =~ "Browser Update.exe"
    or SHA256 in (CampaignHashes)
    or InitiatingProcessSHA256 in (CampaignHashes)
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Downloads\", @"\Temp\", @"\AppData\Local\Temp\")
    or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("explorer.exe","7zg.exe","7zfm.exe","winrar.exe","chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
let CampaignHashes = dynamic(["90aecb370dfb1a99a1f7de0a9c6842ab1b664521fddea16b0ec9a91f322646fc","7aa15de93cf85729ddf970e8d7897f69ece3ca29608f73e784a9ba40c9cea18d","8ecc7108cd679316bf5900e84f19b256dc399902cdede646493f502ac872cc1a","e1ce4e6222396a58d13dddfe64c1dd21f1632bcbe11d1867d44bab4fc646883a"]);
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where ActingProcessName endswith "Browser Update.exe"
    or TargetProcessName endswith "Browser Update.exe"
    or SHA256 in (CampaignHashes)
| where TargetProcessName has_any (@"\Downloads\", @"\Temp\", @"\AppData\Local\Temp\")
    or ParentProcessName has_any ("explorer.exe","winrar.exe","7zg.exe","chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] ClickFix PowerShell pasted from browser-originated clipboard (Run dialog chain) Exploitation High
Detects the ClickFix social-engineering chain: an explorer.exe (Win+R Run dialog) or browser process spawning powershell.exe / cmd.exe with telltale ClickFix payload patterns (mshta-fetched JS, curl/iex/IWR pipelines) that the victim pasted from a malicious 'verification' page. Pivots on the article's PowerShell-execution Phase 3 description. Rationale: Article Phase 3 explicitly cites 'powershell.exe spawned from explorer.exe or a browser parent shortly after a clipboard write' as the ClickFix execution shape, and the campaign's PowerShell payloads reach back to the 8 named injection/TDS domains in the article. The parent + child + cmdline-substring triad is exactly the high-fidelity pivot the BluRaven 'pattern-process-tree' anchor calls for. Cross-checked against: • https://www.silentpush.com/blog/drivesurge/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/004/
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1204.004

[LLM] DriveSurge campaign IP beaconing post-payload execution Command & Control High
Detects outbound TCP/HTTP connections to the four DriveSurge C2/TDS IPs (91.92.240.127, 46.226.166.57, 147.45.42.200, 147.45.42.205) initiated by non-browser processes — i.e. the post-install beacon shape that follows the FakeUpdate or ClickFix execution stage. Rationale: Four campaign IPs are explicitly provided as zTDS/payload infrastructure. Excluding browser-initiated traffic isolates the post-execution beacon (loader/stealer/CS) from the upstream loader fetch already covered by UC #1. Cross-checked against: • https://www.silentpush.com/blog/drivesurge/ • https://otx.alienvault.com/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1105
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
let CampaignIPs = dynamic(["91.92.240.127","46.226.166.57","147.45.42.200","147.45.42.205"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where RemoteIP in (CampaignIPs)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe","vivaldi.exe","yandex.exe","safari.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl
| order by Timestamp desc
let CampaignIPs = dynamic(["91.92.240.127","46.226.166.57","147.45.42.200","147.45.42.205"]);
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where DstIpAddr in (CampaignIPs)
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, SrcUsername, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, NetworkProtocol, Url
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] macOS ClickFix clipboard-hijack: Terminal/osascript shell exec from browser context Exploitation Medium
Detects the macOS variant of ClickFix where a 'verification' page hijacks the clipboard and tricks the user into pasting an attacker-supplied curl/bash one-liner into Terminal. Targets Defender for Endpoint macOS process telemetry — Terminal or osascript spawning bash/sh/zsh with curl + pipe-to-sh sequences shortly after a browser was active. Rationale: Article Phase 5 explicitly calls out the macOS ClickFix variant 'hijacks the clipboard' and Phase 3 lists 'osascript spawned from explorer.exe or a browser parent shortly after a clipboard write' plus 'curl, base64, or sh -c sequences' as the detection hint. Parent (browser/Terminal) + child (shell) + command-substring (curl|sh, base64 -d, do shell script) is the high-fidelity triad. Cross-checked against: • https://www.silentpush.com/blog/drivesurge/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1204.004 T1115
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where DeviceId in ((DeviceInfo | where OSPlatform == "macOS" | distinct DeviceId))
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("Terminal","iTerm2","osascript","Safari","Google Chrome","firefox","Brave Browser","Microsoft Edge")
| where FileName in~ ("bash","sh","zsh","curl","osascript","wget")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("curl -s","curl -sS","curl -fsSL","| sh","| bash","| zsh","base64 -d","base64 --decode","do shell script","eval $(curl")
   or ProcessCommandLine has_all ("curl","http","|")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DvcOs has "mac" or DvcOs has "darwin"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("Terminal","iTerm2","osascript","Safari","Google Chrome","firefox","Brave Browser","Microsoft Edge")
| where TargetProcessName has_any ("bash","sh","zsh","curl","osascript","wget")
| where TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("curl -s","curl -sS","curl -fsSL","| sh","| bash","| zsh","base64 -d","base64 --decode","do shell script","eval $(curl")
   or (TargetProcessCommandLine has "curl" and TargetProcessCommandLine has "http" and TargetProcessCommandLine has "|")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:(linux.auditd OR macos.endpoint) (@process.parent.name:(Terminal OR iTerm2 OR osascript OR Safari OR "Google Chrome" OR firefox OR "Brave Browser" OR "Microsoft Edge") AND @process.name:(bash OR sh OR zsh OR curl OR osascript OR wget) AND @process.command_line:(*"curl -fsSL"* OR *"curl -s"* OR *"| sh"* OR *"| bash"* OR *"base64 -d"* OR *"do shell script"*))

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc

``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("90aecb370dfb1a99a1f7de0a9c6842ab1b664521fddea16b0ec9a91f322646fc", "7aa15de93cf85729ddf970e8d7897f69ece3ca29608f73e784a9ba40c9cea18d", "8ecc7108cd679316bf5900e84f19b256dc399902cdede646493f502ac872cc1a", "e1ce4e6222396a58d13dddfe64c1dd21f1632bcbe11d1867d44bab4fc646883a") or SHA1 in~ ("90aecb370dfb1a99a1f7de0a9c6842ab1b664521fddea16b0ec9a91f322646fc", "7aa15de93cf85729ddf970e8d7897f69ece3ca29608f73e784a9ba40c9cea18d", "8ecc7108cd679316bf5900e84f19b256dc399902cdede646493f502ac872cc1a", "e1ce4e6222396a58d13dddfe64c1dd21f1632bcbe11d1867d44bab4fc646883a") or MD5 in~ ("90aecb370dfb1a99a1f7de0a9c6842ab1b664521fddea16b0ec9a91f322646fc", "7aa15de93cf85729ddf970e8d7897f69ece3ca29608f73e784a9ba40c9cea18d", "8ecc7108cd679316bf5900e84f19b256dc399902cdede646493f502ac872cc1a", "e1ce4e6222396a58d13dddfe64c1dd21f1632bcbe11d1867d44bab4fc646883a")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("90aecb370dfb1a99a1f7de0a9c6842ab1b664521fddea16b0ec9a91f322646fc", "7aa15de93cf85729ddf970e8d7897f69ece3ca29608f73e784a9ba40c9cea18d", "8ecc7108cd679316bf5900e84f19b256dc399902cdede646493f502ac872cc1a", "e1ce4e6222396a58d13dddfe64c1dd21f1632bcbe11d1867d44bab4fc646883a") or SHA1 in~ ("90aecb370dfb1a99a1f7de0a9c6842ab1b664521fddea16b0ec9a91f322646fc", "7aa15de93cf85729ddf970e8d7897f69ece3ca29608f73e784a9ba40c9cea18d", "8ecc7108cd679316bf5900e84f19b256dc399902cdede646493f502ac872cc1a", "e1ce4e6222396a58d13dddfe64c1dd21f1632bcbe11d1867d44bab4fc646883a") or MD5 in~ ("90aecb370dfb1a99a1f7de0a9c6842ab1b664521fddea16b0ec9a91f322646fc", "7aa15de93cf85729ddf970e8d7897f69ece3ca29608f73e784a9ba40c9cea18d", "8ecc7108cd679316bf5900e84f19b256dc399902cdede646493f502ac872cc1a", "e1ce4e6222396a58d13dddfe64c1dd21f1632bcbe11d1867d44bab4fc646883a")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["90aecb370dfb1a99a1f7de0a9c6842ab1b664521fddea16b0ec9a91f322646fc", "7aa15de93cf85729ddf970e8d7897f69ece3ca29608f73e784a9ba40c9cea18d", "8ecc7108cd679316bf5900e84f19b256dc399902cdede646493f502ac872cc1a", "e1ce4e6222396a58d13dddfe64c1dd21f1632bcbe11d1867d44bab4fc646883a"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Miasma Supply Chain Attack Compromises Red Hat npm Packages with Credential-Stealing Worm

The Hacker NewsBleepingComputerStepSecurity
2026-06-01 11 use cases 3 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

Several packages in the @redhat-cloud-services npm scope were found to carry malicious payloads that fire via a preinstall hook on every npm install. The affected versions span multiple packages across the RedHat Cloud Services frontend ecosystem. The payload is a sophisticated multi-stage credential harvester that targets GitHub Actions secrets, AWS, GCP, Azure, Kubernetes, HashiCorp Vault, npm tokens, and CircleCI tokens

Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Node-driven Bun runtime download from oven-sh GitHub Releases during npm install · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Stage-4 implant written to /tmp/p<random>.js and executed by freshly dropped Bun binary · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Miasma Supply Chain Attack Compromises Red Hat npm Packages with Credential-Stea
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] npm preinstall executing oversized index.js from @redhat-cloud-services scope · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] CI runner reading cloud-provider credential env files immediately after npm install
[LLM] npm preinstall executing oversized index.js from @redhat-cloud-services scope Installation High
Hunts for the Miasma supply-chain payload entry point: npm install spawning `node index.js` for a package under `node_modules/@redhat-cloud-services/`, where index.js is unusually large (~4.2 MB). Legit libraries in this scope ship tiny CJS/ESM entry files; a multi-MB index.js is the immediate static anomaly the researchers flagged. Rationale: Anchors on three article-specific facts: the `@redhat-cloud-services` npm scope, an `index.js` entrypoint at npm install time, and the 4.2 MB index size (using 512 KB as a conservative anomaly floor — legit JS entry files are typically <50 KB). Parent-process filter ensures we catch the preinstall-hook execution path, not arbitrary node invocations. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/RedHatInsights/javascript-clients/issues/492 • https://github.com/RedHatInsights/frontend-components/issues/2329
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.007
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
let LookbackDays = 14d;
let ScopePath = @"node_modules\@redhat-cloud-services\";
let ScopePathNix = "node_modules/@redhat-cloud-services/";
let HeavyDrop = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where (FolderPath has ScopePath or FolderPath has ScopePathNix)
    | where FileName =~ "index.js"
    | where FileSize > 524288
    | project DropTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileSize, SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("npm","npm-cli.js","yarn","pnpm","npm.cmd","node.exe","node")
| where FileName in~ ("node.exe","node")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "index.js"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "@redhat-cloud-services" or ProcessCommandLine has ScopePath or ProcessCommandLine has ScopePathNix
| join kind=inner HeavyDrop on DeviceId
| where DropTime between (Timestamp - 5m .. Timestamp + 5m)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, IndexPath = FolderPath1, IndexSize = FileSize, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
let LookbackDays = 14d;
let ScopeWin = @"node_modules\@redhat-cloud-services\";
let ScopeNix = "node_modules/@redhat-cloud-services/";
let HeavyDrop = ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where EventType == "FileCreated" or EventType == "FileModified"
    | where (TargetFilePath has ScopeWin or TargetFilePath has ScopeNix)
    | where TargetFileName =~ "index.js"
    | where TargetFileSize > 524288
    | project DropTime = TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSize, TargetFileSHA256;
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("npm","npm-cli.js","yarn","pnpm","npm.cmd","node.exe","node")
| where TargetProcessName has_any ("node.exe","node")
| where TargetProcessCommandLine has "index.js"
| where TargetProcessCommandLine has "@redhat-cloud-services"
| join kind=inner HeavyDrop on DvcHostname
| where DropTime between (TimeGenerated - 5m .. TimeGenerated + 5m)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSize, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Node-driven Bun runtime download from oven-sh GitHub Releases during npm install Delivery High
Detects the Miasma Stage-3 `_b` downloader: the malicious package's node process fetches the legitimate Bun v1.3.13 binary from the official oven-sh GitHub Releases CDN, drops it under /tmp, and uses it to execute Stage-4. The Bun-from-GitHub-during-npm-install pattern is the smoking gun — legit npm scripts almost never pull alt runtimes mid-install. Rationale: Article explicitly names Bun v1.3.13 fetched from the official GitHub releases CDN by the `_b` Stage-3 downloader, then dropped under /tmp/<random>/. Pairing the node-initiated network fetch with a /tmp Bun binary drop in a short window eliminates dev-machine FPs where engineers install Bun manually via curl. ImWebSession used on Sentinel side (HttpHostName + Url are real columns, unlike SrcProcessName which was the prior error). Cross-checked against: • https://bun.sh/docs/installation • https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/tag/bun-v1.3.13
ATT&CKT1105 T1027 T1140
Data sourcesWeb.Web Network_Traffic.All_Traffic Endpoint.Filesystem

    | where FolderPath startswith "/tmp/" or FolderPath has @"\Temp\"
    | where FileName =~ "bun" or FileName =~ "bun.exe" or FileName endswith ".tar.gz" and FileName has "bun-v1.3.13"
    | project DropTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, DropPath = FolderPath, DropFile = FileName, DropSHA256 = SHA256, DropInitiator = InitiatingProcessFileName, DropInitiatorCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine;
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","node")
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("github.com/oven-sh/bun","objects.githubusercontent.com","release-assets.githubusercontent.com")
   and RemoteUrl has "bun-v1.3.13"
| join kind=inner BunDrop on DeviceId
| where DropTime between (Timestamp - 2m .. Timestamp + 5m)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, DropPath, DropFile, DropSHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
let LookbackDays = 14d;
let BunDrop = ImFileEvent

    | where TargetFileName =~ "bun" or TargetFileName =~ "bun.exe" or (TargetFileName endswith ".tar.gz" and TargetFileName has "bun-v1.3.13")
    | project DropTime = TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, DropPath = TargetFilePath, DropFile = TargetFileName, DropSHA256 = TargetFileSHA256, DropActor = ActingProcessName;
ImWebSession

[LLM] Stage-4 implant written to /tmp/p<random>.js and executed by freshly dropped Bun binary Exploitation High
Detects the Miasma Stage-4 execution handoff: a randomly-named JS file at `/tmp/p<random>.js` (the decrypted 634 KB obfuscator.io payload) being executed by the Bun binary that the downloader just dropped under /tmp. This parent→child shape is article-specific and impossible to legitimately reproduce in normal CI. Rationale: Article explicitly states `_p` is written to `/tmp/p<random>.js` and executed via the freshly downloaded Bun binary — both paths are pinned to /tmp, parent is node, child is bun, and the JS filename matches `p[a-z0-9]+.js`. Regex on the cmdline anchors the random-naming convention without over-fitting on a specific suffix.

| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"/tmp/p[A-Za-z0-9]{3,}\.js"
   or ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"\\Temp\\p[A-Za-z0-9]{3,}\.js"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc

[LLM] CI runner reading cloud-provider credential env files immediately after npm install Actions on Objectives Medium
Hunts the Miasma credential-harvest stage: the Stage-4 implant enumerates GitHub Actions secrets, AWS, GCP, Azure, Kubernetes, HashiCorp Vault, npm, and CircleCI credential locations. Detects node/bun processes reading the well-known credential paths within minutes of an npm install on the same host, which is highly anomalous on CI runners. Rationale: Article enumerates the exact secret stores the implant harvests (GitHub Actions, AWS, GCP, Azure, Kubernetes, HashiCorp Vault, npm tokens, CircleCI). I include the canonical credential file paths for each + GitHub Actions runner internals (`_runner_file_commands`, `RUNNER_TOKEN`). DistinctTargets >= 2 cuts noise from a single legitimate AWS CLI in a JS test. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1552/001/ • https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`

    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time

Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) Exploitation High
Browser-pasted PowerShell launched from explorer/Run dialog — ClickFix social engineering.

Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents

SecurityEvent

title: FakeCaptcha / ClickFix - Clipboard-Injected PowerShell from Explorer
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d06
status: experimental
description: |
    "FakeCaptcha" / "ClickFix" social-engineering: malicious site asks
    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1204.002
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\explorer.exe'
            - '\RuntimeBroker.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
    selection_cmd:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'iex'
            - 'invoke-expression'
            - 'frombase64'
            - 'downloadstring'
            - 'hxxp'
            - 'curl '
            - 'wget '
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_cmd
falsepositives:
    - IT-driven scripted automation that admins paste-launch
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium

| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"

   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |

    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("ba2c6ddb3672bdd6a611e6850b4f700b52aed3dab2f1b3d5f8c839d4a157a709", "4c26cf9791bce1bfd4b84eba80ce2754", "ec514c074caf0ffdce6c66a0e95753d8", "5b26508dc0f1075a7c0b4d8aa464487e") or SHA1 in~ ("ba2c6ddb3672bdd6a611e6850b4f700b52aed3dab2f1b3d5f8c839d4a157a709", "4c26cf9791bce1bfd4b84eba80ce2754", "ec514c074caf0ffdce6c66a0e95753d8", "5b26508dc0f1075a7c0b4d8aa464487e") or MD5 in~ ("ba2c6ddb3672bdd6a611e6850b4f700b52aed3dab2f1b3d5f8c839d4a157a709", "4c26cf9791bce1bfd4b84eba80ce2754", "ec514c074caf0ffdce6c66a0e95753d8", "5b26508dc0f1075a7c0b4d8aa464487e")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("ba2c6ddb3672bdd6a611e6850b4f700b52aed3dab2f1b3d5f8c839d4a157a709", "4c26cf9791bce1bfd4b84eba80ce2754", "ec514c074caf0ffdce6c66a0e95753d8", "5b26508dc0f1075a7c0b4d8aa464487e") or SHA1 in~ ("ba2c6ddb3672bdd6a611e6850b4f700b52aed3dab2f1b3d5f8c839d4a157a709", "4c26cf9791bce1bfd4b84eba80ce2754", "ec514c074caf0ffdce6c66a0e95753d8", "5b26508dc0f1075a7c0b4d8aa464487e") or MD5 in~ ("ba2c6ddb3672bdd6a611e6850b4f700b52aed3dab2f1b3d5f8c839d4a157a709", "4c26cf9791bce1bfd4b84eba80ce2754", "ec514c074caf0ffdce6c66a0e95753d8", "5b26508dc0f1075a7c0b4d8aa464487e")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["ba2c6ddb3672bdd6a611e6850b4f700b52aed3dab2f1b3d5f8c839d4a157a709", "4c26cf9791bce1bfd4b84eba80ce2754", "ec514c074caf0ffdce6c66a0e95753d8", "5b26508dc0f1075a7c0b4d8aa464487e"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

BleepingComputer
2026-06-01 4 use cases 2 techniques 3 kill-chain phases detected

Multiple Dashlane users have been locked out of their accounts following brute-force attacks that attempted logins from distant locations and unknown devices. [...]

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Dashlane brute-force lockout / new-device verification emails to corporate mailboxes (May-Jun 2026 campaign)
[LLM] Dashlane brute-force lockout / new-device verification emails to corporate mailboxes (May-Jun 2026 campaign) Actions on Objectives Medium
Identifies corporate users who received legitimate Dashlane suspension or new-device verification emails during the May 31 - Jun 1 2026 brute-force campaign. These mails (e.g. 'Your account has been temporarily suspended for security reasons...didn't enter the correct token after several tries') mean the attacker reached the account-targeting stage at Dashlane's auth tier for that user; the SOC should proactively rotate the user's master password, revoke active sessions, and watch the user for follow-on phishing. Rationale: Anchors on article-specific signals: Dashlane sender domain (dashlane.com / mail.dashlane.com), May 31 2026 campaign start window per Dashlane status page, and Dashlane's exact suspension-mail phrasing reported by The Register / Help Net Security ('Your account has been temporarily suspended ... didn't enter the correct token after several tries'). Aggregating per-recipient with EmailCount >= 2 raises confidence that the user was actively targeted (one-off legit new-device setup will normally produce one mail, not several). Cross-checked Dashlane status page (status.dashlane.com), The Register and Help Net Security write-ups confirming KR/RU source IPs and email phrasing; skipped image fetch since the in-article notice.jpeg is a UI screenshot of the same Dashlane email already quoted in the body. Cross-checked against: • https://www.theregister.com/security/2026/06/01/password-manager-dashlane-suspends-customer-accounts-amid-brute-force-attacks/5248991 • https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/06/01/dashlane-brute-force-attack-user-accounts/ • https://cyberinsider.com/dashlane-hit-by-brute-force-campaign-triggering-account-suspensions/ • https://status.dashlane.com/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1110/003/
ATT&CKT1110 T1110.003 T1078.004
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email
let CampaignStart = datetime(2026-05-31T00:00:00Z);
let DashlaneDomains = dynamic(["dashlane.com","mail.dashlane.com","notify.dashlane.com"]);
let DashlaneSubjectTokens = dynamic(["suspended","verification code","new device","verify your","sign-in attempt","temporarily suspended","didn't enter the correct token"]);
EmailEvents
| where Timestamp > CampaignStart - 1d and Timestamp < CampaignStart + 14d
| where SenderFromDomain in~ (DashlaneDomains)
   or SenderMailFromDomain in~ (DashlaneDomains)
| where Subject has_any (DashlaneSubjectTokens)
   or Subject has_any ("Dashlane", "new sign-in")
| where DeliveryAction in~ ("Delivered", "DeliveredAsSpam")
| summarize EmailCount = count(),
            FirstSeen = min(Timestamp),
            LastSeen  = max(Timestamp),
            Subjects  = make_set(Subject, 10),
            Senders   = make_set(SenderFromAddress, 5),
            MsgIds    = make_set(NetworkMessageId, 10)
        by RecipientEmailAddress
| extend WindowHours = datetime_diff('hour', LastSeen, FirstSeen)
| extend RiskNote = case(
        EmailCount >= 3, "3+ Dashlane brute-force notifications - very likely targeted",
        EmailCount == 2, "2 Dashlane notifications - investigate user",
        "single Dashlane notification - confirm with user")
| order by EmailCount desc, LastSeen desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc

| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.

Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Office Application Spawning Script Host
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d07
status: experimental
description: |
