[LLM] UnityPlayer.dll side-loaded by RuntimeBroker_update.exe (RUSTCLOAK) Installation High
Detects the DLL side-loading step where the Dragon Weave loader RuntimeBroker_update.exe loads a malicious UnityPlayer.dll from its own directory (instead of from a Unity-engine application context). The combination is article-specific and not seen in legitimate Unity game/app installs. Rationale: Article describes the exact side-load pair: 'the executable loads a malicious DLL (UnityPlayer.dll) via DLL side-loading'. Pairing the parent binary name with the loaded module name produces a single-event signature with effectively zero legitimate co-occurrence (Unity games ship UnityPlayer.dll but the host process is the game's branded EXE, never RuntimeBroker_update.exe). Cross-checked against: • https://www.seqrite.com/blog/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1574/002/
ATT&CKT1574.002 T1027.009
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceImageLoadEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName =~ "UnityPlayer.dll"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "RuntimeBroker_update.exe"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessSHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessName has "RuntimeBroker_update.exe"
| project ProcTime = TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessId
| join kind=inner (
    ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where TargetFileName =~ "UnityPlayer.dll"
    | project FileTime = TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256, ActingProcessName
) on DvcHostname
| where abs(datetime_diff('second', FileTime, ProcTime)) < 600
| project FileTime, ProcTime, DvcHostname, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256

[LLM] AZUREVEIL AdaptixC2 dead-drop to Azure Blob Storage from atypical process Command & Control Medium
Detects the AZUREVEIL C2 pattern: traffic to *.blob.core.windows.net originated by the Dragon Weave loader RuntimeBroker_update.exe or by a process whose image is in a user-writable directory (not from legitimate Azure SDK clients, AzCopy, browsers, or Office). The dead-drop model means both attacker and victim PUT/GET to the same container. Rationale: Article: 'The malware just talks to Azure Blob Storage' and uses 'a dead drop approach' where 'the attacker and the infected system never communicate directly'. Detection couples the legitimate-looking blob.core.windows.net destination with an unusual originating process (the named loader, or any EXE from user-writable directories that isn't a known Azure/storage tool). Pivots on context — blob storage alone is everywhere, but blob storage from a user-temp EXE is rare. Cross-checked against: • https://www.seqrite.com/blog/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1102/003/
ATT&CKT1102.003 T1071.001 T1567.002
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Endpoint.Processes
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteUrl endswith ".blob.core.windows.net" or RemoteUrl contains ".blob.core.windows.net/"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "RuntimeBroker_update.exe"
   or (InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "C:\\Users\\" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "C:\\ProgramData\\" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "C:\\Windows\\Temp\\")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("azcopy.exe","StorageExplorer.exe","msedge.exe","chrome.exe","firefox.exe","onedrive.exe","teams.exe","outlook.exe","excel.exe","winword.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessSHA256, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
let window = 1d;
let blobConn = ImNetworkSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(window)
    | where Url has "blob.core.windows.net" or DstHostname endswith ".blob.core.windows.net"
    | project NetTime = TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, Url, DstHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber;
let suspProc = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(window)
    | where TargetProcessName has "RuntimeBroker_update.exe"
       or ActingProcessName has "RuntimeBroker_update.exe"
    | project ProcTime = TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetProcessName, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessCommandLine;
suspProc
| join kind=inner blobConn on DvcHostname
| where abs(datetime_diff('second', NetTime, ProcTime)) < 600
| project NetTime, ProcTime, DvcHostname, TargetProcessName, ActingProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, Url, DstHostname, DstIpAddr
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:3 (@DestinationHostname:*.blob.core.windows.net OR @QueryName:*.blob.core.windows.net) @Image:(*\\RuntimeBroker_update.exe OR *\\runtimebroker_update.exe OR *\\Users\\* OR *\\ProgramData\\* OR *\\Windows\\Temp\\*) -@Image:(*\\azcopy.exe OR *\\StorageExplorer.exe OR *\\msedge.exe OR *\\chrome.exe OR *\\firefox.exe OR *\\OneDrive.exe OR *\\teams.exe OR *\\outlook.exe)
#event_simpleName=DnsRequest
| DomainName=/\.blob\.core\.windows\.net$/i
| join({#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 (ImageFileName=/\\RuntimeBroker_update\.exe$/i OR ImageFileName=/\\Users\\.*\.exe$/i OR ImageFileName=/\\ProgramData\\.*\.exe$/i OR ImageFileName=/\\Windows\\Temp\\.*\.exe$/i) NOT ImageFileName=/\\(azcopy|StorageExplorer|msedge|chrome|firefox|OneDrive|teams|outlook)\.exe$/i}, field=[aid, ContextProcessId], include=[ImageFileName, CommandLine])
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, DomainName, ImageFileName], function=count())
CLOUD
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(All_Traffic.dest) as dest values(All_Traffic.dest_port) as port values(All_Traffic.bytes_in) as bin values(All_Traffic.bytes_out) as bout from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where All_Traffic.dest_host="*.blob.core.windows.net" by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.app All_Traffic.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | where match(process_name,"(?i)RuntimeBroker_update\.exe") OR NOT match(process_name,"(?i)^(azcopy|storageexplorer|msedge|chrome|firefox|onedrive|teams|outlook|excel|word|powerpnt|powershell|pwsh|az\.exe|aws|backup)")
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(All_Traffic.dest) as dest values(All_Traffic.dest_port) as port values(All_Traffic.bytes_in) as bin values(All_Traffic.bytes_out) as bout from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where All_Traffic.dest_host="*.blob.core.windows.net" by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.app All_Traffic.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | where match(process_name,"(?i)RuntimeBroker_update\.exe") OR NOT match(process_name,"(?i)^(azcopy|storageexplorer|msedge|chrome|firefox|onedrive|teams|outlook|excel|word|powerpnt|powershell|pwsh|az\.exe|aws|backup)")
[LLM] Operation Dragon Weave SHA256 IOC match (RUSTCLOAK/AZUREVEIL/RuntimeBroker_update) Installation High
Hash-based detection covering the 8 SHA256 IOCs Seqrite published for Operation Dragon Weave. Triggers on process execution, file write, image load, or AV scan finding of any of the campaign hashes — provides a fail-safe even if attackers rename binaries. Rationale: Eight SHA256 IOCs were extracted from the article body. Hash-based detection is the most resilient indicator since attackers may rename RuntimeBroker_update.exe or UnityPlayer.dll but cannot mutate the bytes without recompiling. Running against process creation, file write, and image load tables maximises coverage across the full kill chain. Cross-checked against: • https://www.seqrite.com/blog/ • https://bazaar.abuse.ch/
ATT&CKT1027 T1105

  "096372d19b4787e989f44e04c5ecc29885aa927c34ae8666628d6c0eb20bb447",

  "080ab9bc2893ba7bad354551604a667af40ed2ae2d042d2323c2bd9ad3122192",
  "5ed14c2b7f7433a1a72dd6b668413f935a217ba10b69d89b774a82990fa12fe1",
  "61f7d9cd2d8ce7df950639b23ce90085b300b0c6dd0d8d934bba8fdecb670f15",
  "24aa4e780ccd66cef13da9ef98c32954105cf2a32ec643efab0ba1aa2d6352f4",
  "02542a49b3bd6bd2795afb67840acb4557b17e017f7503dd03ebe3aeeb28720e",
  "8ae7c82a3e4f742777e590b25a1c563d19bd9bcba2a387d004aae72c4b2828f9"
]);
union
  (DeviceProcessEvents
   | where Timestamp > ago(90d)
   | where SHA256 in (DragonWeaveHashes) or InitiatingProcessSHA256 in (DragonWeaveHashes)
   | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents", FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, ProcessCommandLine),
  (DeviceFileEvents
   | where Timestamp > ago(90d)
   | where SHA256 in (DragonWeaveHashes)
   | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName, Source = "DeviceFileEvents", FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, ProcessCommandLine = InitiatingProcessCommandLine),
  (DeviceImageLoadEvents
   | where Timestamp > ago(90d)
   | where SHA256 in (DragonWeaveHashes)
   | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName, Source = "DeviceImageLoadEvents", FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, ProcessCommandLine = InitiatingProcessCommandLine)
| order by Timestamp desc
let DragonWeaveHashes = dynamic([
  "096372d19b4787e989f44e04c5ecc29885aa927c34ae8666628d6c0eb20bb447",
  "1c56228cbd1bdebb9e5ea55c2749150fee06c865ede4a3754e8bd6843e51d2d4",

  "5ed14c2b7f7433a1a72dd6b668413f935a217ba10b69d89b774a82990fa12fe1",
  "61f7d9cd2d8ce7df950639b23ce90085b300b0c6dd0d8d934bba8fdecb670f15",
  "24aa4e780ccd66cef13da9ef98c32954105cf2a32ec643efab0ba1aa2d6352f4",
  "02542a49b3bd6bd2795afb67840acb4557b17e017f7503dd03ebe3aeeb28720e",
  "8ae7c82a3e4f742777e590b25a1c563d19bd9bcba2a387d004aae72c4b2828f9"
]);
union
  (ImProcessCreate
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
   | where SHA256 in (DragonWeaveHashes)
   | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, Source = "ImProcessCreate", TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, SHA256),
  (ImFileEvent
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
   | where TargetFileSHA256 in (DragonWeaveHashes)

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
| tstats summariesonly=false count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process Exploitation High

| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)

| where Account !endswith "$"

   or ParentProcessName endswith "\excel.exe"

title: Office Application Spawning Script Host
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d07
status: experimental
description: |
    Word/Excel/Outlook/OneNote spawning powershell, cmd, wscript,
    cscript, mshta, rundll32, regsvr32 — classic macro / embedded-
    object payload signature.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/001/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059
    - attack.t1566.001
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\winword.exe'
            - '\excel.exe'
            - '\powerpnt.exe'
            - '\outlook.exe'
            - '\onenote.exe'
            - '\mspub.exe'
            - '\visio.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate automation macros in trusted internal documents
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
OAuth consent / suspicious app grant Actions on Objectives High
Cloud identity abuse: app gets high-priv scopes, often via consent phishing.
ATT&CKT1528 T1098.001
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication CloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("Consent to application.","Add OAuth2PermissionGrant.","Add delegated permission grant.")
| project Timestamp, AccountObjectId, AccountDisplayName, ActivityType,
          ActivityObjects, IPAddress, UserAgent
// Entra ID directory audit — user / admin consent to a third-party app.
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName has "Consent to application"
| where Result =~ "success"
| extend AppName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName),
         AppId   = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].id),
         User    = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, User, AppName, AppId, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Entra ID Consent to Third-Party OAuth Application
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d05
status: experimental
description: |
    User-driven consent to a third-party OAuth application — illicit-
    consent attack precursor. Pair with first-time-seen-app heuristic
    in your SIEM for higher fidelity.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1528/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1528
    - attack.persistence
logsource:
    product: azure
    service: auditlogs
detection:
    selection:
        OperationName: 'Consent to application'
        Result: 'success'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate first-time SaaS app onboarding
level: medium
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Authentication.Authentication
    where Authentication.action="success"
      AND Authentication.signature IN (
        "Consent to application",
        "Add app role assignment grant to user",

title: FakeCaptcha / ClickFix - Clipboard-Injected PowerShell from Explorer
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d06
status: experimental
description: |
    "FakeCaptcha" / "ClickFix" social-engineering: malicious site asks
    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1204.002
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\explorer.exe'
            - '\RuntimeBroker.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
    selection_cmd:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'iex'
            - 'invoke-expression'
            - 'frombase64'
            - 'downloadstring'
            - 'hxxp'
            - 'curl '
            - 'wget '
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_cmd
falsepositives:
    - IT-driven scripted automation that admins paste-launch
level: high

      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes

| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

[LLM] Egress to codexui-android C2 domain anyclaw.store Actions on Objectives High
Detects DNS resolution or HTTP/S egress to the attacker-controlled C2 domain (sentry.anyclaw.store and parent anyclaw.store) used by the codexui-android npm package and BrutalStrike Android apps to exfiltrate OpenAI Codex OAuth tokens (access_token, refresh_token, id_token, account ID) to the /startlog endpoint. Domain registered 2026-04-12 with no legitimate use case. Rationale: Pivots on the single attacker-controlled C2 domain anyclaw.store (parent of sentry.anyclaw.store/startlog) named in the Aikido blog and corroborated by hackread, cybernews, and the friuns2/codex-mobile GitHub issue #198. Domain registered 2026-04-12 with no legitimate purpose — any internal resolution or HTTP hit is high-fidelity. Covers both Linux dev workstations (where the npm package runs) and Android-emulator/Termux-PRoot traffic from BrutalStrike's apps. Cross-checked against: • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/codex-remote-ui-steals-ai-tokens • https://hackread.com/codex-ui-tool-secretly-stole-openai-refresh-tokens/ • https://cybernews.com/security/openai-codex-tool-malware-token-theft/ • https://github.com/friuns2/codex-mobile/issues/198
ATT&CKT1567 T1071.001 T1071.004 T1195.002

| where RemoteUrl has "anyclaw.store" or RemoteUrl endswith ".anyclaw.store"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true

    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)

    | where Url has "anyclaw.store" or HttpHostName has "anyclaw.store" or DstHostname has "anyclaw.store"
    | project TimeGenerated, SrcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, Url, HttpHostName, HttpMethod, _ResourceId),
  (CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where RequestURL has "anyclaw.store" or DestinationHostName has "anyclaw.store"
    | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, SourceUserName, SourceHostName, RequestURL, DestinationHostName, RequestMethod, DeviceProduct)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Non-Codex process reads ~/.codex/auth.json OAuth token file Actions on Objectives Medium
Detects file events on the OpenAI Codex plaintext OAuth token store (~/.codex/auth.json) by processes other than the legitimate codex CLI/IDE. The compromised codexui-android npm package reads this file out of its Node.js / PRoot sandbox and exfiltrates the access_token, refresh_token, id_token, and account ID. The refresh_token is non-expiring — a single read = persistent account compromise. Rationale: Pivots on the exact plaintext-token path OpenAI documents (~/.codex/auth.json) and explicitly warns about in their support docs (quoted in the article). Aikido confirms the npm package reads this file out of its sandbox before shipping the OAuth blob. Allowlists known-legitimate readers (codex CLI itself, plus node.exe running @openai/codex which is the official CLI's own invocation) so the survivors are credential-stealer candidates. FP-rate medium because IDE indexers and dev shells may occasionally touch the file. Cross-checked against: • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/codex-remote-ui-steals-ai-tokens • https://hackread.com/codex-ui-tool-secretly-stole-openai-refresh-tokens/ • https://github.com/friuns2/codex-mobile/issues/198
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1555 T1528

DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName =~ "auth.json"
| where FolderPath has @"\.codex\" or FolderPath has "/.codex/" or FolderPath has @"\.codex\auth.json"
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed","FileMoved")
| where not(InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("codex.exe","codex","code.exe","cursor.exe"))
| where not(InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","node") and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("@openai/codex","\\codex\\bin\\","/codex/bin/"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFileName =~ "auth.json"
| where TargetFilePath has @".codex\" or TargetFilePath has "/.codex/"
| where not(ActingProcessName has_any ("codex.exe","\\codex","/codex"))
| where not(ActingProcessName has_any ("node","node.exe") and ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("@openai/codex","codex/bin"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Suspicious Access to OpenAI Codex auth.json by Non-Codex Process
id: a7d2b3c4-5e6f-4a1b-9c8d-2e3f4a5b6c7d
description: Detects file events on ~/.codex/auth.json by a process that is not the legitimate Codex CLI / IDE extension, indicating possible OAuth refresh-token theft (codexui-android supply chain attack).
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/openai-codex-authentication-tokens.html
  - https://www.aikido.dev/blog/codex-remote-ui-steals-ai-tokens
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/01
tags:
  - attack.credential_access
  - attack.t1552.001
  - attack.t1528
logsource:
  category: file_event
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '\.codex\auth.json'
      - '/.codex/auth.json'
  filter_codex_cli:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\codex.exe'
      - '/codex'
  filter_codex_node:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\node.exe'
      - '/node'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '@openai/codex'
      - 'codex/bin'
  condition: selection and not 1 of filter_*
level: high
source:(windows.sysmon OR linux.auditd) AND (@TargetFilename:(*\\.codex\\auth.json OR *.codex/auth.json) OR @file.path:(*.codex/auth.json* OR *\\.codex\\auth.json*)) AND NOT @Image:(*\\codex.exe OR */codex OR */Codex.app/*) AND NOT @process.executable.path:(*/codex OR */codex.exe)
#event_simpleName=/^(FileOpenInfo|FileWritten|FileRenameInfo)$/ TargetFileName=/[\\\/]\.codex[\\\/]auth\.json$/i
| NOT (ContextImageFileName=/[\\\/]codex(\.exe)?$/i)
| NOT (ContextImageFileName=/[\\\/]node(\.exe)?$/i AND regex("@openai/codex|codex/bin", field=ContextCommandLine))
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName], function=count())
| sort(_count, order=desc)

[LLM] Installation of malicious codexui-android npm package Installation High
Detects developer workstations installing the compromised codexui-android npm package (any version >=0.1.82 carries the exfiltration code per Aikido). Covers npm/yarn/pnpm CLI invocations as well as on-disk artefacts in node_modules. Author npm account: friuns (Igor Levochkin). Rationale: Pivots on the exact npm package name 'codexui-android' (Aikido's primary IOC, confirmed in friuns2/codex-mobile issue #198 and multiple secondary outlets). The package name is unique enough that any install invocation is high-fidelity; combining cmdline match with the package-manager binary set rules out incidental text mentions in logs or chat scrapes. node_modules path check on DeviceFileEvents catches installs that happened before logging was on (the package has been malicious since version 0.1.82, ~30 days). Cross-checked against: • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/codex-remote-ui-steals-ai-tokens • https://hackread.com/codex-ui-tool-secretly-stole-openai-refresh-tokens/ • https://cybernews.com/security/openai-codex-tool-malware-token-theft/ • https://github.com/friuns2/codex-mobile/issues/198
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.007 T1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
union
  (DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(60d)
    | where ProcessCommandLine has "codexui-android"
    | where FileName in~ ("npm.exe","npm","node.exe","node","yarn.exe","yarn","pnpm.exe","pnpm","npx.exe","npx")
          or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("npm.exe","node.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","npx.exe")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, EventKind="process"),
  (DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(60d)
    | where FolderPath has @"\node_modules\codexui-android" or FolderPath has "/node_modules/codexui-android"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine="", FolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, EventKind="file")
| order by Timestamp desc
union
  (ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(60d)
    | where ActingProcessCommandLine has "codexui-android"
    | where ActingProcessName has_any ("npm","node","yarn","pnpm","npx")
          or ParentProcessName has_any ("npm","yarn","pnpm","npx")
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, EventKind="process"),
  (SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(60d)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where CommandLine has "codexui-android"
    | where NewProcessName has_any ("npm","node","yarn","pnpm","npx")
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname=Computer, ActorUsername=SubjectUserName, ActingProcessName=NewProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine=CommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine="", EventKind="4688"),
  (ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(60d)
    | where TargetFilePath has "node_modules" and TargetFilePath has "codexui-android"
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine=ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName="", ParentProcessCommandLine="", EventKind="file")
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
| tstats summariesonly=false count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]

OAuth consent / suspicious app grant Actions on Objectives High

          ActivityObjects, IPAddress, UserAgent

AuditLogs

| where Result =~ "success"
| extend AppName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName),
         AppId   = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].id),
         User    = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, User, AppName, AppId, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Miasma supply chain attack: malicious code found in @redhat-cloud-services npm packages

Snyk
2026-06-01 4 use cases 4 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

A supply chain worm dubbed Miasma has been found in dozens of @redhat-cloud-services npm releases. The malicious preinstall hook steals credentials, probes cloud identities, and can republish other packages.

ATT&CKT1027 T1190 T1195.002 T1555.003

Detected

Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Miasma supply chain attack: malicious code found in @redhat-cloud-services npm p
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
OAuth consent / suspicious app grant Actions on Objectives High
Cloud identity abuse: app gets high-priv scopes, often via consent phishing.

Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication CloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)

| project Timestamp, AccountObjectId, AccountDisplayName, ActivityType,
          ActivityObjects, IPAddress, UserAgent
// Entra ID directory audit — user / admin consent to a third-party app.
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName has "Consent to application"
| where Result =~ "success"
| extend AppName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName),

| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, User, AppName, AppId, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2024-21182")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate

[LLM] WP Maps Pro CVE-2026-8732 exploit - admin-ajax.php wpgmp_temp_access_support with check_temp=false Exploitation High
Detects the exact exploitation signature of CVE-2026-8732: an unauthenticated HTTP POST to /wp-admin/admin-ajax.php carrying action=wpgmp_temp_access_support and check_temp=false. The plugin's wpgmp_temp_access_ajax_callback() handler is registered with wp_ajax_nopriv_ so any external client can reach it; with check_temp=false it unconditionally invokes wp_insert_user() and creates a rogue WordPress administrator. Wordfence/Defiant observed 3,600+ such requests in 24h on May 30-31 2026. Rationale: Both literal strings (action=wpgmp_temp_access_support and check_temp=false) come from the Wordfence advisory and the kill-chain Phase 1/2 detection hints; requiring both in one request eliminates generic admin-ajax noise. Defender/Falcon/CloudWatch empty because WordPress AJAX exploitation is web-tier and Defender XDR / FDR / CloudTrail don't carry HTTP request bodies for non-AWS-hosted WP sites. Cross-checked against the NVD CVE record, Wordfence Intelligence advisory, and the CyberExpress write-up which independently confirm the action name wpgmp_temp_access_support and the wp_ajax_nopriv_ registration. Cross-checked against: • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-8732 • https://thecyberexpress.com/wp-maps-pro-vulnerability/ • https://www.wordfence.com/threat-intel/vulnerabilities/wordpress-plugins/wp-google-maps • https://www.itsecuritynews.info/15000-wordpress-sites-affected-by-administrator-account-creation-vulnerability-in-wp-maps-pro-wordpress-plugin/

[LLM] WP Maps Pro CVE-2026-8732 follow-up - wp-admin access from IP that previously POSTed wpgmp_temp_access_support Actions on Objectives Medium
Temporal-correlation hunt that confirms successful CVE-2026-8732 exploitation: the same source IP that sent the exploit POST to admin-ajax.php (action=wpgmp_temp_access_support) subsequently retrieves /wp-admin/ pages within an hour, indicating the magic login URL was visited and an authenticated administrator session was established without ever submitting credentials to wp-login.php. Distinguishes scanning noise from confirmed site takeover. Rationale: The exploit POST and the magic-URL-driven admin access from the same source IP is the smoking gun for confirmed compromise (vs the 3,600 daily scanning attempts in the article that never landed). The 1h temporal window matches typical attacker latency between mass-scanning hit and manual followup. Sigma omitted because this is a cross-event join, not a single-event-shape detection. Defender/Falcon/CloudWatch empty because WordPress web-tier visibility doesn't naturally land in those telemetries. Cross-checked against: • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-8732 • https://thecyberexpress.com/wp-maps-pro-vulnerability/

[LLM] PROXYLIB SDK enrollment — first-time DNS lookup of lumiapps.io / asocks.com from a device Installation High
Hunts the moment a device first resolves PROXYLIB / Asocks proxyware SDK domains, indicating fresh enrollment into the residential-proxy botnet. Uses a 30-day anti-join baseline so the alert fires on novel-per-device contact, not legitimate traffic that has already been observed. Rationale: lumiapps.io, asocks.com and bproxy.one are the three domains directly attributed by NCSC/NL Times and the HUMAN Satori PROXYLIB report to the seized residential-proxy infrastructure. A 30-day anti-join baseline is used because a device that has been calling these domains for weeks is already part of the botnet — the operational signal is the first per-device hit. Cross-checked against HUMAN's Satori PROXYLIB write-up which names LumiApps/Asocks as the proxyware vendors. Cross-checked against: • https://www.humansecurity.com/learn/blog/satori-threat-intelligence-alert-proxylib-and-lumiapps-transform-mobile-devices-into-proxy-nodes • https://nltimes.nl/2026/05/dutch-police-take-down-asocks-residential-proxy-botnet • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1090/002/

[LLM] PROXYLIB / Asocks proxyware — process-attributed beacon from non-browser binary Command & Control High
Hunts outbound network connections to PROXYLIB / Asocks proxy botnet infrastructure (asocks.com, lumiapps.io, bproxy.one) where the initiating process is NOT a known web browser. This catches trojanized native applications or embedded proxyware SDKs that have turned a corporate endpoint into a residential exit node for criminal customers. Rationale: Restricting to the three Asocks/PROXYLIB domains plus a NOT-browser predicate yields a near-zero-FP combination: a legitimate user reaching these domains would do so in Chrome/Edge/Firefox; a non-browser binary reaching them means an embedded proxyware SDK or trojanized application is enrolling the host as a residential exit node. Domains corroborated by HUMAN Satori PROXYLIB report and NL Times coverage of the Dutch Politie takedown. Cross-checked against: • https://www.humansecurity.com/learn/blog/satori-threat-intelligence-alert-proxylib-and-lumiapps-transform-mobile-devices-into-proxy-nodes • https://nltimes.nl/2026/05/dutch-police-take-down-asocks-residential-proxy-botnet • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1090/002/
ATT&CKT1090.002 T1071.001 T1583.003
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
let Proxyware = dynamic(["asocks.com", "lumiapps.io", "bproxy.one"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any (Proxyware)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","iexplore.exe","opera.exe","safari.exe","vivaldi.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| summarize ConnectionCount = count(),
            FirstSeen = min(Timestamp),
            LastSeen = max(Timestamp),
            DistinctPorts = make_set(RemotePort, 10),
            SampleCmd = any(InitiatingProcessCommandLine),
            SampleHash = any(InitiatingProcessSHA256)
    by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName,
       InitiatingProcessFolderPath, RemoteUrl
| order by ConnectionCount desc
let Proxyware = dynamic(["asocks.com", "lumiapps.io", "bproxy.one"]);
let Browsers = dynamic(["chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","iexplore.exe","opera.exe","safari.exe","vivaldi.exe"]);
WindowsEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where Provider == "Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon" and EventID == 3
| extend EvData = parse_json(tostring(EventData))
| extend Image = tolower(tostring(EvData.Image)),
         CommandLine = tostring(EvData.CommandLine),
         User = tostring(EvData.User),
         DestinationHostname = tolower(tostring(EvData.DestinationHostname)),
         DestinationIp = tostring(EvData.DestinationIp),
         DestinationPort = toint(EvData.DestinationPort)
| where DestinationHostname has_any (Proxyware)
| extend ImageName = tostring(split(Image, "\\")[-1])
| where ImageName !in (Browsers)
| where User !endswith "$"
| summarize ConnectionCount = count(),
            FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated),
            LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated),
            DistinctPorts = make_set(DestinationPort, 10),
            SampleCmd = any(CommandLine)
    by Computer, User, Image, DestinationHostname
| order by ConnectionCount desc
title: PROXYLIB / Asocks Proxyware Beacon From Non-Browser Process
id: b2c3d4e5-f6a7-4890-9bcd-ef0123456789
description: Detects outbound connections to PROXYLIB / Asocks proxy botnet infrastructure (asocks.com, lumiapps.io, bproxy.one) originating from a non-browser process — strongly suggestive of a trojanized application or embedded proxyware SDK turning the host into a residential exit node.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/dutch-authorities-dismantle-botnet.html
  - https://www.humansecurity.com/learn/blog/satori-threat-intelligence-alert-proxylib-and-lumiapps-transform-mobile-devices-into-proxy-nodes
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/31
tags:
  - attack.command_and_control
  - attack.t1090.002
  - attack.t1071.001
logsource:
  category: network_connection
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    DestinationHostname|endswith:
      - 'asocks.com'
      - 'lumiapps.io'
      - 'bproxy.one'
  filter_browser:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\chrome.exe'
      - '\msedge.exe'
      - '\firefox.exe'
      - '\brave.exe'
      - '\iexplore.exe'
      - '\opera.exe'
      - '\vivaldi.exe'
      - '\safari.exe'
  condition: selection and not filter_browser
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:3 @DestinationHostname:(*asocks.com OR *lumiapps.io OR *bproxy.one OR *Asocks.com OR *LumiApps.io) -@Image:(*\\chrome.exe OR *\\msedge.exe OR *\\firefox.exe OR *\\brave.exe OR *\\iexplore.exe OR *\\opera.exe OR *\\vivaldi.exe OR *\\Chrome.exe OR *\\MsEdge.exe OR *\\Firefox.exe OR *\\Brave.exe)
#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/(^|\.)(asocks\.com|lumiapps\.io|bproxy\.one)$/i
| ContextImageFileName!=/\\(chrome|msedge|firefox|brave|iexplore|opera|safari|vivaldi)\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, DomainName], function=count())
| count > 0
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime sum(All_Traffic.bytes_out) as bytes_out values(All_Traffic.dest_port) as dest_ports from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where (All_Traffic.dest_host="*asocks.com" OR All_Traffic.dest_host="*lumiapps.io" OR All_Traffic.dest_host="*bproxy.one") by host, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.process_name, All_Traffic.process, All_Traffic.dest_host, All_Traffic.user | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | where NOT match(process_name, "(?i)(chrome|msedge|firefox|brave|iexplore|opera|safari|vivaldi)\.exe$") | eval firstTimeStr=strftime(firstTime,"%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S") | eval lastTimeStr=strftime(lastTime,"%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S") | sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime sum(All_Traffic.bytes_out) as bytes_out values(All_Traffic.dest_port) as dest_ports from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where (All_Traffic.dest_host="*asocks.com" OR All_Traffic.dest_host="*lumiapps.io" OR All_Traffic.dest_host="*bproxy.one") by host, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.process_name, All_Traffic.process, All_Traffic.dest_host, All_Traffic.user | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | where NOT match(process_name, "(?i)(chrome|msedge|firefox|brave|iexplore|opera|safari|vivaldi)\.exe$") | eval firstTimeStr=strftime(firstTime,"%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S") | eval lastTimeStr=strftime(lastTime,"%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S") | sort - count
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`

| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
| tstats summariesonly=false count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]

title: Office Application Spawning Script Host

tags:

detection:

        ParentImage|endswith:

            - '\onenote.exe'

OAuth consent / suspicious app grant Actions on Objectives High
Cloud identity abuse: app gets high-priv scopes, often via consent phishing.
ATT&CKT1528 T1098.001
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication CloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("Consent to application.","Add OAuth2PermissionGrant.","Add delegated permission grant.")
| project Timestamp, AccountObjectId, AccountDisplayName, ActivityType,
          ActivityObjects, IPAddress, UserAgent
// Entra ID directory audit — user / admin consent to a third-party app.
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName has "Consent to application"
| where Result =~ "success"
| extend AppName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName),
         AppId   = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].id),
         User    = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, User, AppName, AppId, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Entra ID Consent to Third-Party OAuth Application
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d05
status: experimental

[LLM] PAN GlobalProtect inbound from Vultr/Dromatics IOC IPs (CVE-2026-0257) Delivery High
Detects inbound connections to GlobalProtect portal/gateway (TCP/443) from the specific Vultr and Dromatics Systems IPs Rapid7 attributed to CVE-2026-0257 cookie-forgery exploitation starting May 17, 2026. Pivot: a hit on these IPs against any internet-facing PAN-OS appliance is high-confidence pre/active exploitation. Rationale: Uses the four CVE-2026-0257 attacker IPs Rapid7 attributed to Vultr and Dromatics Systems; pivot is exact IP match on TCP/443 to a PAN appliance, so FP rate is effectively zero unless the same IPs host legitimate pentest infra. Cross-checked against Rapid7's published analysis referenced in the article and the CISA KEV listing dated 2026-05-29. Cross-checked against: • https://www.rapid7.com/blog/ • https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog • https://security.paloaltonetworks.com/
